label: Steamed cheese (parenica)
note: Slovak and Goral cheeses: matured lump cheese is scalded and stretched; not the same as oscypek, which is pressed in wooden moulds and smoked, not stretched.

about.text: Steamed cheese is the Slovak way of turning matured sheep lump cheese into a plastic mass by working it in hot water, then pulling it into ribbons or strings. Parenica is wound into spirals, korbáčik braided; both are usually smoked and are traditionally sheep, now often cow.

how.text: The lump cheese is already soured by its day of fermentation, so it stretches in hot water without any extra acid, the way pasta filata curd does.

steps.note: Pieces of about 500 g are worked in a wooden vessel of 60–70 °C water.

steps.name: pull
steps.note: With a wooden spatula into a ribbon about 4–6 m long and 6 cm wide.

steps.name: smoke
steps.note: Smoked, though an unsmoked version exists.

processing.text: This is the lump cheese that is steamed: milk at 32 C with rennet and lactic bacteria (species not named), curd left to ferment for about a day. It is already soured, so it stretches in hot water without extra acid.
